properties.Comments: 200-acre borrow area to be used for initial nourishment at North Ponte Vedra Beach; design excavation depth of -52 ft NAVD88; median grain size = 0.25mm; mean grain size = 0.28mm; sorting = 0.81phi; fine to medium quartz sand w/ minor carbonate/shell content; avg carbonate content by acid digestion = 7.4%; only 0.56% by weight, on avg, retained on #4 sieve; fines content passing #230 sieve = 1.73%; avg Munsell value of 6.7; avg Munsell chroma of 1.0; avg Dean overfill ratio of 1.34 compared to existing beaches
properties.Citation: Tidewater Atlantic Research Inc., Vol I: Phase I Submerged Cultural Resource Remote-Sensing Survey of a Potential Offshore Borrow Area, Eight Temporary Pipeline Corridors and Assessment of Previously Identified Terrestrial Sites in the Project Nourishment Area of Potential Effect. September 2020.

properties.Comments: 196-acre borrow area to be used for renourishment at North Ponte Vedra Beach; design excavation depth of -52 ft NAVD88; median grain size = 0.26mm; mean grain size = 0.29mm; sorting = 0.89phi; fine to medium quartz sand w/ some shell, only slightly shellier material than borrow area A; avg carbonate content by acid digestion = 9.3%; only 0.81% by weight, on avg, retained on #4 sieve; fines content passing #230 sieve = 1.82%; avg Munsell value of 6.9; avg Munsell chroma of 1.0; avg Dean overfill ratio of 1.22 compared to existing beaches
properties.Citation: Tidewater Atlantic Research Inc., Vol I: Phase I Submerged Cultural Resource Remote-Sensing Survey of a Potential Offshore Borrow Area, Eight Temporary Pipeline Corridors and Assessment of Previously Identified Terrestrial Sites in the Project Nourishment Area of Potential Effect. September 2020.

properties.Comments: derived from the primary cut in 2006 Offshore Geophysical and Geotechnical Report Figure 8; total volume from Table 7; sand unit thickness 10-20ft; Primary dredge cut to a depth of nine to ten feet is recommended
properties.Citation: Offshore Geophysical and Geotechnical Report; Raccoon Island Shoreline Protection/Marsh Creation Project Phase B (TE-48), June 2006

properties.Comments: Compatible sand layer at core locations ranged from 8-12ft in thickness; avg phi sorting = 0.68; avg % retained on #4 sieve = 0.4; avg % visual shell = 1.4;  Considerable volume of beach quality sand with various possible borrow area configurations.  Recommend further exploration of SJ-3 for design phase.
properties.Citation: Taylor Engineering Inc., Northern St. Johns County Offshore Sand Resource Investigation; Reconnaissance Phase Geotechnical Exploration Report. August 2019

properties.Comments: Beach quality sand primarily located within a narrow strip along the crest of the shoal. Compatible sand layer at core locations ranged from 5-8ft in thickness. avg phi sorting = 0.96; avg % retained on #4 sieve = 1.4; avg % visual shell = 3.2; Volume estimate will likely decrease upon further investigation. SJ-2 like more suitable for future nourishment projects due to limited volume.
properties.Citation: Taylor Engineering Inc., Northern St. Johns County Offshore Sand Resource Investigation; Reconnaissance Phase Geotechnical Exploration Report. August 2019

properties.Comments: Minimal amount of beach quality sand; most samples analyzed did not comply with color and silt content criteria; see report for details.

properties.Comments: Low linear shoal trending northeast. Core 194 near the southwest end recovered 9 feet of clean fine to medium quartz sand with thin layers of varying size. Composite sand from this site may be satifactory for nearby beaches. Needs further investigation.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments:
Core 191 at the extreme end of a long low ridge contains suitable sand with a mean diameter of 0.380 mm (1.4 phi) in the upper 2 feet. The material in core 191 is fine gained below -2 feet and it is doubtful if any but the surficial material will be suitable. Need further investigation.

properties.Comments: Core 16 at the nortllwest edge of this low linear ridge atop a bank shoal contains clean quartz sand with a median diameter ranging from 0.330 to 0.268 mm (1.6 to 1.9 phi). Core 76 was only 3 feet long so it is not known is the ridge contains similar material at depth. Seismic evidence suggests that the sand is 10 feet or more in thickness.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments:
Cores taken throughout this extensive area off Jacksonville Beach generally contained a thin surficial layer of clean, medium to coarse quartz sand; upper 2 feet coarser than deeper material. Suitable borrow site may exist but sand is probably too thin in many areas. Best material was in cores 78. 79, and 185 in the eastern part of this area. Needs further investigation.

properties.Comments: Volume estimated for channel deposit. Cores 48 and 65 located over the 'ancient channel' of the St. Johns River contained reasonably clean, medium to coarse quartz sand under a shallow overburden of type F sand. This material may represent a deposition in the old channel. Further exploration may be most productive along the central part of the channel area southeast of core 48; cores to the NW indicate the channel is filled with mud.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments: Large, irregular, low relief shoal where geophysical records indicate formation via accretion (possibly during last transgression). If so, this is an exception as most similar shoals off N. FL appear to be erosional remnants. The few cores from the highest part of the shoal recovered up to 10 ft of clean, med-coarse quartz sand. Highest central part are considered the best prospects.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments: Two cores penetrated a clean medium quartz sand layer 4 to 6 feet thick. A ridge-like feature near core 123 is judged to be the most likely locale for a suitable borrow area.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments:
Clean type A sand over 10 feet thick with mean diameters ranging from 0.287 to 0.308 mm (1.9 to 1.8 phi) was recovered by core 140 in the center of this linear shoal. Prospects for locating suitable borrow areas in this ridge are judged to be very good.

properties.Comments: Core 141 in this irregular low relief shoal area contained over 11 feet of clean uniform med sand with an avg mean diameter ranging from 0.287 to 0.308 mm (1.7 to 1.8 phi). Suitable borrow areas should exist near core 147 and probably occur throughout the main ridge area.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments: The surface sand in core 1493 from this long narrow ridge is a clean med quartz sand ranging from 0.233 to 0.308 millimeters (1.4 to 2.1 phi) mean diameter. Below about 2 feet, similar but slightly silty sand extends to 7 feet. The quality of the material in this area does not appear to be as good as sand in areas A-8 and A-9. Total vol estimate for entire ridge is 5 mcy but only 1.5 mcy are probably suitable for beach fill.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments: Low, roughly linear shoal lying parallel to shore off Amelia Island may contain thick sand accumulations. No core data available. properties.Comments: Large, triangular-shaped closed depression in which cores indicate the top of the type M sediment layer outcrops or is at sllallow depth (< 5 feet) and thus accessible to dredges. Type M sand in cores from this area is generally of coarse texture and has a dolomite silt matrix.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments: Core 190 is in a small closed depression and contains 11 feet of type M sediment which outcrops at the core site and may be exposed throughout the depression. The core contains a mixture of coarse quartz sand with a dolomite silt matrix.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments: Extensive, area covering a broad, ridge-like feature with subtle relief appears to be underlain by type M sediment. Cores in this area generally encountered the sediment at 3 feet or less, and outcrops probably occur in many places. An ancient channel bisects the area (A5) and along the channel course type M sediment is deeply buried under channel fill.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments: The type M sediment found in M3 is composed of mostly med to coarse quartz sand in a silty matrix consisting of fine, particulate organic matter or dolomite silt.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments: This area consists of a crook-shaped low ridge. Core 133 near the inshore flank of the ridge contains fine slightly silty sand. It is not known if this sand is typical of sediments in this ridge.

properties.Comments: Core 2 off St. Marys River Entrance at Fernandina contains 5 feet of clean well-sorted fine sand with an avg mean diameter of 0.218 mm (2.2 phi). The core is 5 feet long and terminates in sand; total depth of the deposit is unknown. The deposit is apparently not extensive as surrounding cores do not contain similar material. The material in this deposit may be related to the nearby inlet.
properties.Citation: Meisburger E P, Field M E. 1975. Geomorphology, Shallow Structure and Sediments of the Florida Inner Continental Shelf, Cape Canaveral to Georgia. Technical Memorandum No. 54. Fort Delvain (VA): USACE, Coastal Engineering Research Center. 122 p.

properties.Comments: This area, of unknown extent and depth, is centered on core 11 south of St. Marys River Entrance. The core is 5 feet long and consists of well-sorted, fine-med quartz sand, and is a shallow core representing an upper shoreface locale not sampled elsewhere. The sand deposit may therefore extend laterally along the upper shoreface, but is unlikely to extend seaward since all seaward cores contain fine silty sand.

properties.Comments: Sand deposits in this area were typically thicker than Area A, averaging 30-60 inches and sediment characteristics were more consistent. Median grain size ranged from 0.22 mm to 2.0 mm with the dominant sizes between 0. 25 mm and 0. 50 mm. There were significant concentrations of fine shell hash present in the area, contributing to the larger median grain size.
properties.Citation: USACE Charleston District and SC Department of Health and Environmental Control. February 2017. Joint Public Notice P/N SAC-2017-00179. 17 p.

properties.Comments: Sediment thickness exceeds 4–5 ft, and the material is sand. Known areas of hardbottom exist to the north and the south of the search area, and a swale of lower bathymetry and reduced sediment thickness bisects the area. Borings within the proposed borrow area rang in mean grain size from 0.235mm to 0.321 mm with shell content ranging from 7.8% to 21.3%. The composite grain size for all borings is 0.278 mm with 12% shell.
properties.Citation: USACE Charleston District and SC Department of Health and Environmental Control. October 2020. Joint Public Notice P/N SAC-202000503 (Revised). 21 p.

properties.Comments: Usable sand thickness averages 5.8 ft with a maximum of 15.3 ft. The borrow source consists of poorly-graded sand w/ intermittent thin layers of clay and clayey/silty sands. This layer terminates at -41 ft and is underlain by a mixture of clayey sand and well-graded gravel that ranges in thickness from 3 to 10 ft. Gravel is underlain by high plasticity clay, where the top of the clay unit ranges from -42 to -52 ft.
properties.Citation: Integrated General Reevaluation Report and Environmental Assessment for Coastal Storm Damage Reduction Project, Folly Beach South Carolina, Appendix B - Geotechnical, July 2020

properties.Comments: This borrow area is within a CBRA unit. Usable sand thicknesses reach up to 13.8 ft and average 6.8 ft. Usable sand is underlain by a continuous fat clay and clayey sand at -43 ft.
properties.Citation: Integrated General Reevaluation Report and Environmental Assessment for Coastal Storm Damage Reduction Project, Folly Beach South Carolina, Appendix B - Geotechnical, July 2020

properties.Comments: This borrow area is within a CBRA unit. The volume generated by the Stono Inlet ebb shoal Borrow Area J is ~3.4 Mcy, the complex is noted in the RSM database. When dredged 10 ft, the feasibility study indicates increased wave heights that impact the nearby shorelines. Additional modeling and geotechnical studies must be done to use this ebb shoal complex. When dredged to 10 ft, ~ 12,500,000 cy of material currently lies within Borrow Areas I and J (Stono Inlet Ebb Shoal). This volume estimate does not include infilling.
properties.Citation: Integrated General Reevaluation Report and Environmental Assessment for Coastal Storm Damage Reduction Project, Folly Beach South Carolina, Appendix B - Geotechnical, July 2020

properties.Comments: This is an investigation area within the ebb shoal of the South Edisto River Inlet. It was investigated for the Edisto Beach Coastal Storm Damage Reduction Project. 4 borrow area scenarios were suggested for this investigation area. The potential volume of borrow material under the 4 areas ranges from ~12 mcy to ~18 mcy. The entire sand search area contains potentially almost 30 mcy if excavated to an average of ~7.7 ft. The volume generated by this ebb shoal is included within the RSM analysis.

properties.Comments: Borrow area contains low percentages of gravel (>2 mm diameter) and shell material. While shell content (CaCO3) constitutes ~9 percent of the borrow sediments, only about 1.5 percent is gravel size. This means nearly all the shell material is in the form of sand-sized particles. 2018 plans indicate dredge depths between 2  and 4 ft, assumed a consistent 3 ft depth for initial borrow area volume.

Sand boundary designations were obtained from correlating GLO-UPOCS-VC-24-01-03, 07-09, 11-18, 20-21, 25, 27, 29, 36, 37, 40, 41, 44-46, 50, 59-62 to specific seismic characteristics across regions of unit Q1. Sand percent varies and is likely mixed sediments (30-70% fines). This unit does not have overburden.
